sections.h2: How big is Citrus County and who lives there?
sections.html:
Citrus County spans 581.92 land square miles, and the Census Bureau estimates its population at 171,666 for mid-2025, up 11.6% from 153,843 in 2020.

The age mix leans senior, with 38.1% at 65 or above and 14.2% under 18. Owners occupy 85.2% of the 90,919 housing units, and permits issued in 2025 numbered 2,102.

Median home value is $245,500 for 2020 to 2024, and owners pay a median of $1,354 a month with a mortgage or $447 without. Median household income is $56,546, and 13.5% of people live in poverty. Compared with a county where median homes cost far more, the tax bill itself is smaller, though it still weighs on households living on fixed incomes.

sections.h2: Which Citrus County office does what?
sections.html:
The Citrus County Property Appraiser values property and decides exemptions, and the Citrus County Tax Collector sends bills, takes payment and sells tax certificates.

  • Property appraiser: homestead and other exemption applications, portability, agricultural classification and the August TRIM notice. The office phone is (352) 341-6600.
  • Tax collector: bills, discounts, installment applications and delinquent tax advertising.
  • Clerk: files the deed at closing and collects stamp tax.

The appraiser's site says March 1 is the filing deadline for portability, exemptions, classifications and assessment reductions, and April 1 is the filing deadline for tangible personal property. Owners who buy a home after January 1 are encouraged to pre-file for the next year.

sections.h2: What are the Citrus County tax discounts and due dates?
sections.html:
Bills are collected starting in November, with a 4% discount through November 30, then 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February; March is the full amount and the due date is March 31.

sections.h2: Can I pay Citrus County property tax in installments?
sections.html:
Yes, the county allows quarterly payments. The installment plan requires an application by April 30, and the collector sets the eligibility test as prior year taxes above $100.

The first payment is due June 30 at a 6% discount, and the collector says payments accepted after June 30 but before July 31 are not discounted. The second is due September 30 at 4.5%, the third December 31 at 3%, and the fourth March 31 with no discount. Missing the first payment cancels the plan, and the full tax is then due by March 31.

The first two installments are based on the prior year's tax bill. Changes in ownership, value or exemptions show up in the last two. The collector says enrolled taxpayers are re-enrolled automatically, so a buyer taking over a home with an active plan should ask the office what applies for that year, and a seller should say in the contract who owes which installment.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Citrus County taxes?
sections.html:
They become delinquent on April 1, and a 3% penalty is added to the gross amount.

In May, the collector advertises the delinquent real estate list in the local newspaper once a week for three consecutive weeks, and that cost is added to the bill. The tax certificate sale begins on or before June 1. Unpaid tangible personal property taxes carry a 1.5% penalty after April 1 and are advertised once.

State law lets a holder apply for a tax deed once two years have passed since April 1 of the year the certificate was issued. The owner may redeem the certificate before a deed is issued, and the opening bid at a deed sale includes half of the assessed value for homestead property. Ask the Citrus County Tax Collector for a payoff before you list or close.

sections.h2: How do homestead and Save Our Homes work for a Citrus County owner?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is up to $50,000, and you file with the Citrus County Property Appraiser by March 1 of the year you apply.

The appraiser's page says the first $25,000 applies to all property taxes, and the added $25,000 applies to assessed value over $50,000 and to non-school taxes only. The same page puts the typical savings at roughly $500 a year. After the first year, the assessment cannot rise by more than the lesser of CPI change or 3 percent. If you moved from one Florida homestead to another within three years, you may be able to take some of your Save Our Homes savings along.

The Department of Revenue notes that homestead ends when the owner rents the unit or no longer lives there as a permanent resident. A sale also resets the property to just value on the following January 1.

sections.h2: What does the Census show about work and housing in Citrus County?
sections.html:
Only 40.3% of people aged 16 and over are in the civilian labor force, and the county counts 17,659 veterans. Medical and social assistance receipts reached $1,111,065 thousand in 2022, and retail sales were $2,628,656 thousand, or $16,176 a resident.

There were 3,063 employer establishments and 31,162 paid employees in 2023, and the mean commute is 27.8 minutes. Rent runs a median $1,107, and 88.3% of residents had not moved within the past year.

Rental owners should know that furniture and equipment used in a rental or business is taxed separately as tangible personal property. Returns are due April 1, and unpaid tangible tax carries a 1.5% penalty after April 1.

sections.h2: What changes for a Citrus County seller at closing?
sections.html:
The title company splits the year's tax between buyer and seller and clears any back taxes out of your proceeds before the deed is recorded.

The state's deed stamp tax runs 70 cents per $100 of consideration in most counties, collected at recording, and each party is liable whichever side agrees to pay. Citrus County's older, long-tenured owner base means many sellers hold capped assessments, so the buyer's first bill after a sale often looks different from the seller's last. Before closing, ask for three things.

  • A payoff statement from the tax collector showing current and prior year balances.
  • Confirmation of whether any tax certificate was sold on the parcel.
  • The status of any installment plan, since the plan rolls forward each year.

faqs.q: What is the Citrus County early payment discount?
faqs.a: It is 4% if paid in November, 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February. March payments get no discount, and April 1 is delinquency.

faqs.q: When is the installment application due in Citrus County?
faqs.a: The application is due by April 30, and the first payment is due June 30. Payments after June 30 but before July 31 get no discount.

faqs.q: When does a Citrus County tax bill turn delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1, when a 3% penalty is added to the gross amount. The tax certificate sale begins on or before June 1.

faqs.q: What is the homestead filing deadline in Citrus County?
faqs.a: March 1 of the year you apply. The Citrus County Property Appraiser accepts the application and decides eligibility.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Citrus County house that has delinquent tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Back taxes and fees come out of your proceeds at closing. Get a payoff from the tax collector before closing, and check for a sold certificate.
